name: Hodiah
overview: Hodiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah known primarily for the significant legacy of his sons, who became the fathers of the towns Keilah and Eshtemoa. His mention in Scripture highlights his role within the genealogical and territorial history of Judah. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hodiah is a proper name meaning 'grandeur is y-h-v-h,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors the greatness of the LORD. This name reveals a connection to God's majesty, though it was not given directly by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Hodiah is identified as the grandfather of Keilah and Eshtemoa through his sons, indicating his familial influence in the establishment of these locations. Additionally, he is related by marriage as a brother-in-law to Naham. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Hodiah's significance lies in his genealogical contribution to the tribe of Judah, as his descendants became founders of notable towns within the land. This establishes him as a link in the continuity of God's people and their settlement in Canaan. His mention in 1 Chronicles 4:19 situates him within the broader biblical narrative of God's providential care over His chosen lineage.
